Area Forecast Discussion
National Weather Service Baltimore MD/Washington DC
400 AM EST Tue Nov 24 2026

.WHAT HAS CHANGED...
Have issued a Special Weather Statement for the threat of
elevated fire danger this afternoon. This covers east of U.S. 15
in Maryland. Otherwise, the deep coastal low remains on track
with a myriad of hazards impacting the area for Thanksgiving
Day. Forecast wind gusts remain plagued by uncertainty, but 
conditions will be certainly be windy. 

&&

.KEY MESSAGES...
- 1) A coastal low pressure system will bring heavy rain, strong
  wind gusts, and coastal flooding Thanksgiving Day.

- 2) Cool temperatures through mid-week, with a gradual warming
  trend behind the coastal low this weekend.

&&

.DISCUSSION...
KEY MESSAGE 1...A coastal low pressure system will bring heavy 
rain, strong wind gusts, and coastal flooding Thanksgiving Day.

No significant model trends to report this cycle with respect to the 
coastal storm to impact the Mid-Atlantic coast on Thanksgiving Day. 
Models seem to have honed in on the track just east of I-95 
with only subtle speed differences. 

Latest EPS output now shows a higher prob of 2" of rain south of I-
66 and US-50 that it showed yesterday. Winds showed a slight 
increase in magnitude with gusts of 40-55 mph likely across much of 
the area and gusts as high as 70 mph along the Chesapeake Bay and 
higher elevations due to an intense 925 mb easterly jet of 70kt. 
Minor coastal flooding seems like a safe bet with the potential for 
moderate at Anne Arundel and St. Marys Counties due the strong 
onshore flow combined with high astronomical tides associated with a 
Full Moon today. 

The storm system departs the local area late Thu evening with steady 
rain ending, with showers turning into snow showers across the 
mountains and broken stratocumulus and gusty WSW winds across the 
rest of the area.


KEY MESSAGE 2...Cool temperatures through mid-week, with a
gradual warming trend behind the coastal low this weekend.

Outside of the high-impact coastal system, mainly quiet
conditions are expected through mid-week, and again into the
last weekend of November. 

For the current conditions, the earlier cold front now stretches
from Nova Scotia down to the coastal Carolinas. Any anafrontal
showers have largely shifted just east of the Delmarva
Peninsula. The GOES-19 multi-layer water vapor channel shows
plenty of dry air moving in from the Great Lakes. Some recent
aircraft soundings show that dry air, particularly in the mid-
levels of the troposphere. A decent amount of mixing is still
occurring in the boundary layer which is supported by periodic
gusts up to 15 to 20 mph around the area. This all eventually
sets the stages for a dry and brisk day ahead.

The passage of the upper trough will allow for continued
northerly cold advection today. Forecast highs reach the upper
40s to low 50s, with mainly 30s to low 40s in the mountains.
This is accompanied by abundant sunshine, but with northerly
gusts up to 20 mph. A strong area of Canadian high pressure is
set to move from the Great Lakes toward New England tonight. By
tonight into Wednesday morning, the forecast shows surface
pressures as high as 1041 mb over upstate New York. With the
ridge sagging southward along the spine of the Appalachians, a
cold night looms ahead. Tonight's lows will largely range from
the upper teens to 20s. Areas along and east of I-95 should stay
closer to the freezing mark. Heading into Wednesday, highs
remain fairly close to today, but this comes with increasing
clouds and a shift to northeasterly flow. Such winds pick up in
strength into the night as gusty showers move in from the south.
Overnight gusts around 25 to 35 mph are expected, with up to 45
mph across the mountains. For more information on the
Thanksgiving forecast, please see Key Message 1 (above).

The period spanning Friday and into Saturday sees the coastal
low pushing north of the Mason-Dixon Line into New England.
Tight gradients persist which will keep brisk winds in the
forecast. The net winds are mainly out of the west to southwest
which is not the most favorable for upslope activity along/west
of the Alleghenies. However, still expect some light
accumulations possible throughout Friday into Saturday morning.
For the weekend into early next week, global ensembles show a
slow but steady warm up. Overall precipitation chances appear
meager to finish out the month.

&&

.AVIATION /08Z TUESDAY THROUGH SATURDAY/...
Behind the earlier cold front, intermittent northwesterly gusts
to around 15 knots have been observed early this morning. Winds
gradually shift to northerly today with afternoon gusts up to 
15 knots or so. This comes with VFR conditions that persist the
remainder of the day and into much of Wednesday. As strong high
pressure passes by to the north, expect an increase in
northeasterly winds. Gradients tighten further into Wednesday
night ahead of the potent coastal system arriving for
Thanksgiving Day. Restrictions become likely on Wednesday night
as waves of gusty showers pass through from the south.

The strong East Coast storm to bring significant travel impacts
to aviation Thanksgiving Day with heavy rain, IFR flight 
restrictions, wind gusts of 35-45 kt, and strong LLWS. Rain ends
late Thu evening, but MVFR cigs from broken stratocu and gusty 
WSW winds to continue into Saturday.

&&

.MARINE...
Hazardous conditions are likely to be present over the waterways
for much of the week. Right now, Small Craft Advisories are in
effect with northwesterly gusts up to 20 to 30 knots. Much of
these drop by the early afternoon while continuing until just
dark across the more southern waters. However, near advisory
caliber winds continue throughout the evening and overnight as
winds shift from north to northeasterly. Thus, current Small
Craft Advisories may need to be extended in time. By Wednesday,
gradients tighten further as strong high pressure passes through
New England and low pressure lifts up from the Gulf Coast.
Northeasterly gusts up to 20 to 25 knots are expected.

High likelihood of gale force winds Thu and even a low of risk of 
storm force winds. A Gale Watch remains in effect from late 
Wednesday night through Friday afternoon. Winds remain elevated
through Saturday afternoon which likely warrants Small Craft
Advisories.

&&

.FIRE WEATHER...
Behind an earlier cold front, breezy north to northwest winds 
will increase in strength late this morning through the 
afternoon. This lowers afternoon relative humidities into the 25
to 30 percent range. Winds gradually weaken toward dusk as a 
strong area of Canadian high pressure builds across the Great 
Lakes into New England. 
 
A potent coastal system is expected to bring wet and windy 
conditions Wednesday night into Thanksgiving Day. This will supply
a wetting rain to all locations. Mountain snow showers will occur
on the back side of the low on Friday, while brisk winds 
continue. Temperatures slowly moderate toward the weekend.

&&

.TIDES/COASTAL FLOODING...
While tidal anomalies have fallen in the northwesterly flow, 
astronomical tides are very high with the Full Moon today.
However, there should be no issues during the next 24 to 36
hours.

A strong coastal low pressure area will move up the Eastern 
Seaboard Wednesday into Thanksgiving Day. Depending on the 
evolution and track, tide levels likely rise once again. 
Widespread minor coastal flooding is now expected along the 
tidal Potomac River and western shore of the Chesapeake Bay from
St. Mary's County up to Havre de Grace. A low risk of moderate 
coastal flooding also exists along Anne Arundel and St. Mary's 
Counties' shorelines. 

&&
